items.proposition: Accessible used battery and exposed battery are hazards.
items.formatDefense: Two of five; a dead battery is the realistic near-miss. Prevention scenario, not ingestion treatment.

items.proposition: Assess patient-perceived dyspnea benefit and acute respiratory/sedation safety separately.
items.clinicalBoundary: Explicit prescribed therapeutic trial; no new dose or guarantee of respiratory safety.

items.proposition: Worsening mental status and refill warrant reassessment despite improving other measures.
items.formatDefense: Two of five; falling but still elevated lactate is a realistic trend-vs-normality near-miss. No single test diagnoses sepsis or proves adequate resuscitation.

items.proposition: Rapid multi-electrolyte fall after nutrition supports refeeding; execute prescribed replacement and dextrose reduction.
items.differentialDefense: Weakness/dyspnea/tachycardia during PN can reflect overload, infection or refeeding; fluid assessment and serial electrolytes resolve the offered alternatives. A clean catheter site does not rule out bloodstream infection.
items.clinicalBoundary: Adult, explicit nutrition-team prescription. ASPEN allows individualized reduction/cessation depending on severity; no universal autonomous PN-rate instruction.
items.reviewAttention: Independent reviewer must assess differential competitiveness and the scope of parameters. Magnesium is required safety monitoring, not used as a false distractor.

items.proposition: Breathing pauses/gasps plus functional daytime sleepiness warrant evaluation.
items.formatDefense: Two of five; late TV use is a sleep-hygiene near-miss. No definitive diagnosis from symptoms alone.

items.proposition: New disorientation and hallucination trigger specified escalation.
items.formatDefense: Two of five; common mild symptoms are plausible near-misses. The anxiety segment is explicitly an earlier report, preventing contradiction with current disorientation.
items.clinicalBoundary: No forced treatment sequence or sedative dosing.
